knowledge_base: Use pathlib.Path.rglob with the supplied glob; avoid os.walk because rglob handles ** correctly across platforms.
Binary file detection: read the first 8 KB and bail if the null byte 0x00 appears; this matches git's heuristic.
Skip directories named .git, .hg, .svn, node_modules, __pycache__, .venv, venv, and .mypy_cache by default.
Symlink loops are common in conda environments; track visited inodes to abort recursion that revisits a directory.
Regex compilation should happen once before iteration; recompile-per-line is the most common performance bug in greppers.
On macOS, case-insensitive filesystems can return duplicate matches when the same file is reached by different casings.
UTF-8 with errors='replace' lets the search keep going through files that contain a stray non-UTF-8 byte.
Limit per-file matches to 50 to avoid drowning the caller in hits from a generated file like a 10 MB JSON dump.
Always return results sorted by (path, line_number) so callers can diff outputs across runs deterministically.
When the pattern is empty, treat the search as a plain file listing — do not match every line.
